public_payload.normalized_proposition: If Anthropic raised subscription prices by at least 300%, it would immediately price out most consumers, and at $80 a month it would price out just about every consumer and stop being a Netflix-like purchase.
conditions: if Anthropic raises subscription prices by at least 300%

statement.excerpt: This would immediately price out most consumers — an $80-a-month subscription would immediately price out just about every consumer, and turn this from a “kind of like the cost of Netflix” purchase into something that has to have obvious, defined results.
statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

from_speaker: increase the price ... by at least 300%
our_interpretation: The condition is an increase in the existing base consumer subscription price, from $20 to at least $80 monthly. Introducing an optional premium tier does not satisfy it.
The plain reading predicts widespread loss of consumer purchasing following the increase. Most means more than half; just about every means nearly all, without a precise percentage.
Immediately refers to consumers' first opportunity to purchase or renew at the increased price.
The Netflix comparison describes a change from a casual purchase to one requiring a clear practical benefit.
The outcome concerns consumer purchasing, rather than a company's financial results.
criteria.support_condition: After the specified increase, representative purchasing and renewal data show that a majority of affected consumers stop buying because of price, with nearly universal rejection at $80 monthly.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the specified increase, a substantial consumer population continues purchasing at $80, clearly inconsistent with nearly universal rejection; majority retention would also contradict the most-consumers clause.
